title: Vendor constellation entry-gate verification (gc-08)
context: VI-01 (census repair), VI-02 (PASSPort/Checkbook procurement-spine wiring), and VI-03 (expanded gold + conservative alias policy) landed on main before this measurement. This receipt re-verifies the three entry gates the vendor constellation's promotion decision depends on, plus a live-cohort resolved-same rate VI-03 did not publish (its worker measured gold only).

false_split.method: Same run as precision gate; false_split counted over all 56 gold_v1 cases (43 same-labeled pairs across vendor/agency/procurement).

pair: Quality Construction Group LLC DBA QCG Builders

multi_domain.method: Re-ran the shipped PIN/EPIN join (worker/src/lib/passport_join.mjs) between the committed full award census (site/data/ocp_awards_warehouse_lookup.json, 53,245 rows) and a fresh live pull of PASSPort Public's contractData.js (61,032 contracts, fetched 2026-08-05), then counted distinct vendorStem values that appear in BOTH the award census and the PASSPort-joined subset.

result.definition: share of resolved vendor roots (full award census) carrying an edge in ≥2 money sub-kinds (award + PASSPort/Checkbook contract corroboration)

multi_domain.caveat: This measures multi-sub-kind linkage WITHIN the money domain (award vs. contract corroboration), which is the pairing the task named ('awards + contracts/payments at minimum'). It is not the same denominator as docs/evidence/vendor-footprint-coverage.json's multi_domain_vendor_rate gate, which counts entities matched in >=2 of the 7 cross-domain domains (money/land/property/rules/meetings/people/franchise) inside the capped 200-root entity-intelligence materialization. As of 2026-08-12 the EI graph feed uses the population-backed PASSPort census under a measured 1,550-row cap (see docs/evidence/passport-ei-densify/comparison.json) rather than the prior 2-row compatibility fixture — money multi-kind density inside that graph is now real (contract objects and references_contract edges), while cross-domain multi_domain_vendor_rate can still be low because land/rules/meetings/property/franchise objects remain overwhelmingly agency-identified rather than vendor-identified in this corpus.
multi_domain.passed_note: 27.84% is a meaningful, non-trivial share, but below the 50% bar the diagnosis's own promotion gate used. The constellation ships qualified/labeled, not unqualified, consistent with this result.

live_cohort_resolved_same_rate.label: PASSPort-joined award-PIN cohort — matcher+conservative_v1 policy resolved-same rate
live_cohort_resolved_same_rate.method: Live re-run of the diagnosis's methodology: parsed the live PASSPort Public contractData.js dump with worker/src/lib/passport_parse.mjs, joined it to the committed award census by PIN/EPIN with worker/src/lib/passport_join.mjs (same exact/prefix/suffix rules used in production), then scored every joined pair's vendor-name pair through the deployed pipeline (entity_resolution/features + matchers + policies, conservative_v1). Each side's OWN native key (award PIN vs. PASSPort EPIN) was used for the authority-key feature, so only exact-value joins get an authority-key auto-same; prefix/suffix-bridged rows still had to clear name-similarity matching.
live_cohort_resolved_same_rate.note: The 10 unresolved rows are all weak prefix/suffix joins where the award vendor and PASSPort vendor names are unrelated companies (e.g. 'King Teleservices L.L.C.' vs 'PIVOTPOINT SECURITY INC') — correctly held unresolved rather than auto-linked. This is a measurement over the PIN-joined cohort only, not the full award corpus.
